HallJoy Madlions SafeHID root-cause fix v6 + V9 unthrottled pipeline

Confirmed by the V5 field logs:
- Eight isolated-host crashes occurred in roughly 33 minutes.
- Every crash was 0xC0000005 execute at 0x21.
- Every crash stopped at madlions_before_receive.
- All snapshots before each crash were valid.
- The failure is therefore not Steam-specific and is not a Madlions value/parser overflow.

Root-cause transport rewrite:
- Replaces the old Soup Madlions sequence that overlapped ReadFile and WriteFile
  on one HID handle while both OVERLAPPED structures had hEvent == NULL.
- Uses a dedicated serial request/response state machine for Madlions.
- Drains stale reports, then fully completes the write, then starts the read.
  Read and write are never outstanding at the same time.
- Every OVERLAPPED operation has its own persistent manual-reset event.
- Every pending operation is completed or CancelIoEx-cancelled and drained
  before its OVERLAPPED structure, event, or buffer can be reused.
- Buffers keep a stable address for the complete I/O lifetime.
- Timeouts and Windows transport errors are exported to HallJoy diagnostics.
- Persistent transport errors cause a controlled fresh-process/HID-handle
  restart instead of an access violation or a frozen snapshot.
- The parent clears analog output immediately when a host crash/hang is seen.

Retained safety fixes:
- Bounds-checks every Madlions layout index, including the incomplete final chunk.
- Rejects HID responses shorter than the 27 bytes required by the parser.
- Clears the complete AnalogueKeyboard state union.
- Stores failed-report state per keyboard object.
- Uses a 16-bit layout offset and correct state-count rounding.
- Clamps travel to 0..350 and normalized analog values to 0..1.
- Clears failed chunks so keys cannot remain stuck.
- Uses an RAII cross-process Madlions mutex guard.
- Fixes undefined object-lifetime behavior in Soup HandleRaii move assignment.
- Serializes snapshots and full-buffer release state.
- Disables hotplug for the isolated HallJoy path.
- V9 restores one independent worker per analog device; poll workers have no artificial sleep.
- V9 makes the isolated host publish on fresh-device notifications instead of a fixed 8 ms cadence.
- Bypasses the Wooting SDK dynamic layer and calls private ABI1 directly.
- Keeps process isolation as a final fault-containment boundary.
- Pins Soup to b02796b0b20276277c8a4b4d3759643eeab43ff7.
- Uses optimization plus frame pointers for post-crash analysis.
